KLjgBLwH3Wc.title: Minding your mitochondria | Dr. Terry Wahls | TEDxIowaCity
KLjgBLwH3Wc.summary: Dr. Terry Wahls tells how she used diet to manage her multiple sclerosis and get out of a wheelchair, drawing on mitochondrial biology. TED flagged the talk as health advice based on personal narrative.
KLjgBLwH3Wc.why: HN commenters point to it as a moving personal story that motivated dietary changes, though it is also cited as anecdotal evidence.

quote.text: I highly recommend the talk, it is both very informative and very moving.

qEV9qoup2mQ.title: Alexander Pope Wrote a 35-Page Takedown of a Historian
qEV9qoup2mQ.summary: CGP Grey tells the story of Alexander Pope's long takedown of a historian, Thomas Hearne, framed around the quirks of library books and archival research. It is a funny, digressive video essay about literary feuds and tracking down original sources.
qEV9qoup2mQ.why: HN commenters point to it as a masterpiece of humorous archival detective work and a great watch about books and libraries.

quote.text: Linking the full video because it's a masterpiece

cn7kTPbW6QQ.title: Building Your Own Dynamic Language
cn7kTPbW6QQ.summary: Ian Piumarta's 2007 Stanford EE380 lecture on building a dynamic programming environment from the ground up, from the Viewpoints Research Institute's work. It covers the design of a language and system with a recursive design, parsing through code generation, and the COLA architecture.
cn7kTPbW6QQ.why: HN commenters recommend it as a way to understand what the VPRI group considers core, such as supporting any syntax on one JIT compiler and removing boundaries between application and interpreter.

quote.text: There's a talk by Ian Piumarta that tries to get to the core of what the VPRI guys feel is important.

sK5i-N34im8.title: Cgroups, namespaces, and beyond: what are containers made from?
sK5i-N34im8.summary: Jérôme Petazzoni explains how Linux containers are built from kernel features like cgroups, namespaces and SELinux. He demonstrates putting the pieces together by hand to make a container and compares runtimes and approaches like jails and zones.
sK5i-N34im8.why: HN recommends it as a talk that makes containers click, showing that containerization is not virtualization and demystifying what Docker does.

quote.text: I watched this talk couple of years ago that made docker/containers finally click for me.

uqH_Y1TupoQ.title: Watching This Video Disqualifies You From Jury Duty for Life
uqH_Y1TupoQ.summary: CGP Grey explains jury nullification, a juror's power to acquit despite the law, and why mentioning it can get you struck from jury selection.
uqH_Y1TupoQ.why: HN links it as the clearest short explainer of jury nullification and how the jury system works, often in threads on prosecutors and trials.

SDtAh9IwG-I.title: How big is a visible photon?
SDtAh9IwG-I.summary: Huygens Optics shows through a laser interference experiment that the question of a photon's size is really about coherence length. It argues that photons exist as energy exchanges between radiation and matter, not as little particles in free space.
SDtAh9IwG-I.why: HN recommends it as an approachable, intuitive explanation of why visible photons can be surprisingly large, from a channel known for practical optics.

quote.text: I like this one for the approachable and intuitive explanation

1f6YyH62jFE.title: 37C3 -  Operation Triangulation: What You Get When Attack iPhones of Researchers
1f6YyH62jFE.summary: A 37C3 talk by Kaspersky researchers on Operation Triangulation, a zero-click iPhone attack that targeted their own colleagues. They describe capturing every stage of the chain, four zero-days and a previously unknown spyware active for years.
1f6YyH62jFE.why: HN recommends it as a gripping look at what nation-state attackers can do, used as the primary source in threads about iPhone security and Kaspersky.

quote.text: was a rollercoaster of a ride. If you have the time to watch it I highly recommend it!

dmWQtI3DFFo.title: JuliaRobotics: Making robots walk with Julia | Robin Deits
dmWQtI3DFFo.summary: Robin Deits presents the JuliaRobotics organization and shows how Julia is used to visualize, simulate and control a humanoid robot. The talk touches on real-time performance and composability across packages.
dmWQtI3DFFo.why: Julia fans point to it as a concrete example of Julia working for soft real-time robotics, especially when avoiding heap allocation.

quote.text: There's a nice talk here [1] about using julia in soft-real-time for robotics.

eX9m3g5J-XA.title: 7 Habits For Effective Text Editing 2.0
eX9m3g5J-XA.summary: Vim author Bram Moolenaar's 2007 Google Tech Talk on habits for efficient text editing: find inefficiencies in your own editing, then learn the Vim commands that fix them.
eX9m3g5J-XA.why: Recommended as practical advice straight from Vim's author, and shared in memory of Bram after his death.

quote.text: This video of a talk that Bram Moolenaar (the author of vim) gave at Google in 2007 has some pretty good advice.

iptAkpqjtMQ.title: The Life of a Bolt
iptAkpqjtMQ.summary: Oracle Red Bull Racing follows a single front suspension bolt through its life, from sketch and drawing through machining, testing, assembly and racing.
iptAkpqjtMQ.why: HN commenters cite it as an illustration of the extreme effort Formula One teams put into safety, performance and reliability for a single part.

quote.text: The Life of a Bolt video does a really good job of illustrating just how far these teams will go for safety, performance, and reliability.

OeC1yAaWG34.title: Mongrel Nation - Brown cow
OeC1yAaWG34.summary: A comedy segment where Eddie Izzard travels to Friesland to try speaking Old English, claiming English originated in Holland and buying a cow to prove it.
OeC1yAaWG34.why: HN uses it as a joke reference in threads about the history of the English language.

QDVVo14A_fo.title: Google’s The Selfish Ledger (leaked internal video)
QDVVo14A_fo.summary: Leaked internal Google X video, 'The Selfish Ledger', a speculative thought experiment about treating user data as a ledger that could guide and shape human behavior, including products sold to fill data gaps.
QDVVo14A_fo.why: HN cites it as a glimpse of how Google and other data companies think about behavioral sequencing and data collection.

quote.text: pushing specific products on relevant customers in order to fill gaps in data collection.

QEjdiE0AoCU.title: Emily Howell - Track 1
QEjdiE0AoCU.summary: A short clip of a track from Emily Howell, a computer program by David Cope that composes classical-style music, performed by human players. It is a sample of algorithmic composition.
QEjdiE0AoCU.why: Used as an example of computer-generated music in threads on AI creativity and music.

QHZ48AE3TOI.title: How can less be more?
QHZ48AE3TOI.summary: A very short clip of Yngwie Malmsteen explaining why he thinks the phrase 'less is more' is wrong and that more is more.
QHZ48AE3TOI.why: HN mostly uses it as a joke or punchline in threads about minimalism versus excess.

bct8stbZafI.title: Sean Brock And Anthony Bourdain Eat At The Waffle House
bct8stbZafI.summary: A short clip from Anthony Bourdain's Parts Unknown in which he and chef Sean Brock end a long night of drinking at a Charleston Waffle House. It celebrates the unpretentious, welcoming late-night diner. Bourdain's remark comparing the meal favorably to the French Laundry is what people remember.
bct8stbZafI.why: HN commenters cite it whenever Waffle House comes up, as a touchstone for Bourdain's love of humble, unfancy places.

quote.text: This is better than the French Laundry.

y3InF19dzlM.title: UNBELTED Passenger in Frontal Car Crash
y3InF19dzlM.summary: IIHS frontal crash test footage showing what happens to an unbelted rear-seat passenger. It illustrates that buckling up in the back matters for the passenger and for front occupants.
y3InF19dzlM.why: Used as a visual example in seat belt and personal-freedom debates, showing an unbelted rear passenger becoming a projectile.

quote.text: If you're in the back seat of a car, without a seat belt, in a collision you may turn into a projectile
